item.title: Florida Farm to School Contests Open to Local Students Through November 16
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services is inviting middle and high school students across the state, including those in the Pensacola area, to enter two contests celebrating agriculture's role in schools and communities. The contests run through November 16, 2026, and are part of National Farm to School Month. High school…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services is inviting middle and high school students across the state, including those in the Pensacola area, to enter two contests celebrating agriculture's role in schools and communities. The contests run through November 16, 2026, and are part of National Farm to School Month.

High school students in grades 9–12 can compete in the Essay Contest for college scholarship money. The top prize is $3,000 toward a Florida Investment 529 Plan, with second place earning $2,000 and third place $1,000. The winning essay will be published in a Florida agricultural publication, and the first-place writer will be recognized at the 2027 Florida Farm to School Conference with a travel stipend. This year's essay prompt asks students to imagine themselves as farmers in their own community and describe what they would grow and how their farm would support local schools and neighbors.

Middle school students in grades 6–8 can enter the inaugural Farm to School Art Contest by submitting original 2D artwork celebrating Florida agriculture and its connection to schools and communities. The first-place artwork will be featured on official 2027 Farm to School Month campaign materials, and the winning artist will receive recognition at the conference plus a travel stipend. Honorable mention pieces will be shared across the Farm to School website and the Florida Department of Agriculture's social media channels.

Both contests are open to students in public, private, charter, virtual, and home-school programs. Entries can be submitted at FarmToSchoolFL.com/Contests. According to the Department of Agriculture, the essay contest is now in its third year and is supported by R.C. Hatton Farms, a longtime Farm to School advocate.

item.title: Sen. Rick Scott Introduces Bills to Block Chinese Military Companies from U.S. Stock Exchanges
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: U.S. Senator Rick Scott unveiled two pieces of legislation Wednesday aimed at preventing Chinese Communist Party military companies from trading on American stock exchanges, citing national security and investor protection concerns. The Know Your Sanctioned Securities Act and the Protecting U.S. Investors from Chinese Military Companies Act would…
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Senator Rick Scott unveiled two pieces of legislation Wednesday aimed at preventing Chinese Communist Party military companies from trading on American stock exchanges, citing national security and investor protection concerns.

The Know Your Sanctioned Securities Act and the Protecting U.S. Investors from Chinese Military Companies Act would direct the Securities and Exchange Commission to identify companies linked to China's military and suspend their trading privileges. The first bill would add a "CMC" ticker modifier to flag Chinese military companies; the second would require mandatory trading suspensions within 10 days of the Department of War updating its list of such entities.

"Communist China's military companies want to use U.S. markets and exchanges to fund the CCP's efforts to attack our way of life using dollars from American investors," Scott said in a statement. "We can't let that happen." The legislation has drawn support from the Coalition for a Prosperous America and the American Securities Association, both of which argue that American retirees and savers should not inadvertently fund adversarial military operations through their investment portfolios.

The bills restrict the SEC's regulatory authority to the specific mechanics of implementation, barring the agency from expanding prohibitions or determining which companies qualify for restriction beyond those officially designated by the Department of War.

item.title: Florida Protects 375-Acre Polk County Farm Through State Conservation Program
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida Commissioner of Agriculture Wilton Simpson announced Thursday the permanent protection of Walter Farms, a nearly 375-acre cattle operation in Polk County, through the state's Rural and Family Lands Protection Program. The conservation easement, valued at $3 million with $750,000 contributed by Polk County, prevents future development of…
item.content:encoded:
Florida Commissioner of Agriculture Wilton Simpson announced Thursday the permanent protection of Walter Farms, a nearly 375-acre cattle operation in Polk County, through the state's Rural and Family Lands Protection Program. The conservation easement, valued at $3 million with $750,000 contributed by Polk County, prevents future development of the working farm while allowing agricultural operations to continue.

Walter Farms sits on the northern shore of Gator Lake, with portions dedicated to pasture, agriculture, and nursery plants alongside forested areas. According to the announcement from the Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services, the property's surrounding landscape has largely been converted to agricultural or improved pasture use.

Since its creation in 2001, the Rural and Family Lands Protection Program has preserved more than 251,000 acres of working farmland statewide. Under Simpson's leadership since 2022, the program has protected nearly 186,000 of those acres. The state has secured $1.1 billion in funding for the initiative since 2022, including $425 million allocated in the current budget cycle. The program works by purchasing development rights through easements, allowing farmers to maintain operations while preventing sprawl—and avoiding the higher costs of state-owned conservation land management.

The free event runs from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Sunday, October 18, at Seville Square and Fountain Park in downtown Pensacola. Visitors can expect vendor booths, dog…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Humane Society is gearing up for the 20th anniversary of Barktoberfest, the annual fundraiser bringing dog lovers and families together to support shelter animals. The free event runs from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Sunday, October 18, at Seville Square and Fountain Park in downtown Pensacola.

Visitors can expect vendor booths, dog contests, training demonstrations, food trucks, and beverage options throughout the day. The event doubles as a community awareness push for homeless animals while raising funds to help the Humane Society's shelter dogs and cats find permanent homes.

"Barktoberfest is a chance for people to enjoy a day with their dogs while helping animals that are still waiting for a home," said Mary McClellan, vice president of development for Pensacola Humane Society. The organization is actively recruiting sponsors, vendors, and volunteers for the event.

Those interested in sponsoring, vending, or volunteering can find details at pensacolahumane.org/Barktoberfest or contact the organization at barktoberfest@pensacolahumane.org or 850.748.2471.

item.title: UWF Professor Lands $196K NSF Grant for Microscopic Robotics Research
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: University of West Florida Assistant Professor Minh Quang Ta has secured a $196,215 grant from the National Science Foundation to develop robotic systems capable of manipulating biological cells and microscopic objects with unprecedented precision. The project will focus on creating laser-actuated robotic micro-fingers that work together like a…
item.content:encoded:
University of West Florida Assistant Professor Minh Quang Ta has secured a $196,215 grant from the National Science Foundation to develop robotic systems capable of manipulating biological cells and microscopic objects with unprecedented precision.

The project will focus on creating laser-actuated robotic micro-fingers that work together like a robotic hand, allowing researchers to grasp, move, rotate and roll cells and other microscopic objects. Ta's team will also develop learning algorithms to give the robotic system greater dexterity and flexibility in performing manipulation tasks. The challenge of working at microscopic scales — where objects are extremely small, fragile, and difficult to control — has traditionally required entirely new approaches rather than simply shrinking conventional robotic systems, Ta explained.

The research could ultimately support advances in biomedical research, cell manipulation, lab-on-chip technologies, and precision manufacturing. Beyond the scientific applications, the grant will provide hands-on research and training opportunities for UWF students in robotics, control systems, and interdisciplinary engineering, from concept development through experimental studies. "The grant will strengthen robotics research at UWF and will enhance collaboration opportunities with researchers in biology, biomedical and marine sciences," said Dr. Mohamed Khabou, dean of UWF's Hal Marcus College of Science and Engineering.

The incoming class includes Kailon Cunningham, Seraphina Daly, Caylee Deleo, Camden Fisher, Zachary Galloway, Nafisa Goromo, Nigel Goromo, Victoria Horton, Tamiya Jones,…
item.content:encoded:
Take Stock in Children of Escambia County has selected 25 new scholars for the upcoming school year, drawing students in grades 7 through 10 from schools across the district. The incoming class includes Kailon Cunningham, Seraphina Daly, Caylee Deleo, Camden Fisher, Zachary Galloway, Nafisa Goromo, Nigel Goromo, Victoria Horton, Tamiya Jones, Jamari Kinchen, Gunner Knight, Malena Lopez, D'ior Martin, Jayda McNeill, Lana Mejia, Payson Olford, Devina Persad, Briella Planas, Arhaam Raheem, Jacob Salazar, Aubrii Simmons, Michael Standback, Christopher West, Govinda Willard, and Charles Williamson.

The scholars were celebrated in August at the program's annual Kickoff Dinner & Celebration at The Wright Place, where they received congratulations from Escambia County Superintendent Keith Leonard, State Representative Michelle Salzman, and School Board Member Carissa Bergosh. Take Stock in Children is a 31-year-old nonprofit that pairs eligible, financially and academically qualified middle and high school students with volunteer mentors, college readiness coaches, and college prep resources. Scholars who maintain program standards in academics, attendance, and citizenship through high school graduation receive four-year scholarships covering tuition and fees at Florida's state college rate, with funds also usable for technical and vocational training or university tuition.

The Escambia County affiliate currently supports 177 scholars in grades 7 through 12, with 145 alumni using Take Stock scholarships at post-secondary institutions statewide. The program has helped scholars earn 245 post-secondary degrees and credentials, including associate's, bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees, plus professional certifications. Scholarship funding comes from local donations matched dollar-for-dollar by the Florida Prepaid College Foundation. For information on applying, mentoring, or contributing, contact Alexandra Bach at 850-469-5458 or abach@ecsdfl.us.

item.title: Baptist Health Care, PAM Health Partner to Add 100 Hospital Beds in NW Florida

item.content:encoded:
Baptist Health Care and PAM Health have announced a partnership aimed at expanding healthcare capacity across Northwest Florida, including the Pensacola area. According to WKRG-TV 5, the collaboration will add 100 hospital beds to the region's healthcare infrastructure.

The expansion represents a significant investment in local medical services at a time when hospital capacity and access to care remain priorities for Escambia County residents. Details on the timeline for bed additions, specific facility locations, and the scope of services covered under the partnership were not immediately available.

Baptist Health Care operates multiple facilities throughout the Pensacola area, while PAM Health manages post-acute care services. The partnership underscores ongoing efforts by major healthcare providers to meet growing demand in the region.

item.title: Rain expected today, storms likely Friday through weekend

Today should stay relatively dry until after 1 p.m., when scattered showers and thunderstorms become more likely. The real concern…
item.content:encoded:
A wet pattern is moving into the North Escambia area, with showers possible this afternoon and more significant storms expected to develop Friday through the weekend, according to the National Weather Service forecast.

Today should stay relatively dry until after 1 p.m., when scattered showers and thunderstorms become more likely. The real concern arrives Friday, when numerous to widespread showers and storms are expected across the region.

Some of those storms could produce heavy rainfall capable of causing localized flash flooding, forecasters warn. Residents in low-lying or flood-prone areas should monitor conditions closely through the weekend as the wet weather system moves through.

The increase, championed by Orlando attorney John Morgan, was approved through a constitutional amendment that phased in higher wages over several years. The $15 rate now applies statewide to all covered workers. Employers…
item.content:encoded: Florida's minimum wage officially hit $15 per hour Thursday, completing a series of increases mandated by voters in 2020. The increase, championed by Orlando attorney John Morgan, was approved through a constitutional amendment that phased in higher wages over several years. The $15 rate now applies statewide to all covered workers. Employers across the Pensacola area and throughout Florida are adjusting payroll systems and wage schedules to comply with the new requirement.

item.title: Northwest Florida sheriffs warn of kratom danger after 9 deaths
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Law enforcement agencies across Northwest Florida are issuing a public warning about kratom use following nine deaths reported in the region, according to WPMI NBC 15. Sheriffs' offices in the area say they're concerned about the rising number of fatalities linked to the herbal substance, which is legal in Florida but has faced increased scrutiny…
item.content:encoded:
Law enforcement agencies across Northwest Florida are issuing a public warning about kratom use following nine deaths reported in the region, according to WPMI NBC 15.

Sheriffs' offices in the area say they're concerned about the rising number of fatalities linked to the herbal substance, which is legal in Florida but has faced increased scrutiny from health and law enforcement officials over potential health risks.

The warning comes as kratom use has grown in popularity, particularly among younger adults seeking an alternative to prescription opioids or other substances. The plant-based product is typically consumed as a powder or tea and is sold in convenience stores and specialty shops throughout the region.

Authorities are urging residents to be aware of the potential dangers and are encouraging anyone struggling with substance use to seek help through local treatment resources.

item.dc:creator: newsroom

Duran's testimony addressed a key question in the case: why he did not immediately identify himself outside Fortson's…
item.content:encoded:
Former Okaloosa County Deputy Eddie Duran took the stand Wednesday to explain his actions the day he fatally shot Air Force Airman Roger Fortson in May 2024, telling the court he believed his life was in danger at the time.

Duran's testimony addressed a key question in the case: why he did not immediately identify himself outside Fortson's apartment before the shooting occurred. Body camera footage from the incident was presented during the testimony, according to WKRG News 5.

The case has drawn significant attention given Fortson's military service and the circumstances surrounding the shooting. Duran's account of fearing for his safety represents a central element of the legal proceedings as the case moves through the court system.
